title: Choose the visual world
question: Keep the assigned Technical Dossier, choose an alternate, or ask for another direction.

options.label: Technical Dossier
options.lineage: engineering field notes and decision records
options.thesis: A clear consulting offer presented with the precision of an engineering brief.
options.viewport: Ansh's offer and a system-flow diagram share the first view; verified outcomes anchor the next section.
options.risk: Too much annotation could compete with the offer.

raised.raise: Keep service and outcome labels sharply indexed so visitors can scan the work before reading detail.
Use the whole page as one connected technical record, not a collection of generic cards.

options.label: Systems Atlas
options.thesis: Show how customer data, media, AI, and digital experiences connect to business outcomes.
options.viewport: A service map leads the opening, with the consultant's role and call action attached directly to it.
options.risk: A map can make varied engagements look more uniform than they are.

options.label: Transit Split-Flap Board
options.thesis: Treat services and case evidence as a strict, legible destination board.
options.viewport: A departures-board grid indexes service lanes and case outcomes beside a direct consulting action.
options.case: The row hierarchy makes technical work easy to scan; it carries less of the consultant's cross-functional role.
options.risk: A literal station-board treatment could feel like a travel site.

options.label: Variable Type Specimen
options.thesis: Make a type specimen the primary interactive surface.
options.viewport: A changing display face fills the hero while controls change its weight and width.
options.case: The type interaction draws attention away from consulting services and approved outcomes.
options.kept: Set technical labels and measured data with disciplined hierarchy, without making type controls the product.
options.risk: The page could be mistaken for a font foundry.

options.label: Fold Sequence
options.thesis: Explain the engagement as one continuous folded sequence.
options.viewport: A single fold diagram connects audit, pilot, and scale into one process.
options.case: The physical-fold metaphor does not explain the consultant's data and product work.
options.kept: Keep the real audit-to-pilot-to-scale sequence visible as a concise process.
options.risk: A decorative fold could imply a method more rigid than the engagement.

options.label: Shadow Bazaar
options.thesis: Organize services as a market of ideas and opportunities.
options.viewport: Visitors wander between service stalls and compare their needs with each offering.
options.case: Market language adds an invented metaphor instead of making the technical offer clearer.
options.kept: Make each service route easy to compare and keep its practical scope attached.
options.risk: The visual metaphor would compete with a direct business message.

options.label: Delivery Field Guide
options.thesis: Present each service as a promise paired with instructions.
options.viewport: Service packets arrange what a team gets beside a timeline for delivery.
options.case: The planting metaphor implies a staged product package that the consulting offer does not promise.
options.kept: Pair each service description with a clear scope or next step where the current content supports it.
options.risk: Illustrated crop art has no factual relationship to the work.

options.label: Diagnostic Quiz
options.thesis: Let visitors answer a quiz to reveal the service they need.
options.viewport: A short diagnostic starts in the hero and branches into a recommended service.
options.case: A quiz invents a self-service diagnostic the site does not currently offer.
options.kept: Use the existing contact route for specific needs rather than pretending to diagnose them automatically.
options.risk: A recommendation could overstate what a short questionnaire can know.

canonCard.label: Category-standard consulting site
canonCard.thesis: A polished consulting layout with a direct offer, proof, services, and a call action.
canonCard.viewport: A concise hero, two verified outcomes, a service index, then contact.
canonCard.risk: Clear and familiar, but less distinctive than either technical direction.
